cells.tense: You are working, right now, with the whole shape of it in view.
cells.act: count it out and read what the numbers show
cells.ask: Count the numbers once, plainly, before deciding what they mean — what actually exists, what was spent, what's left. Read the page before the plan gets its turn.
cells.core:
You can hold a whole thing in view at once — all of it, together, nothing off to the side waiting to surprise you. That's how this works: the shape lands complete, and what needs putting in order is already visible in it. When it runs, work finishes in a way people can stand on, because nothing was left hidden.

This is the place where finished things get released, and releasing is part of understanding, not a failure of it. So lay the numbers out once — counted, not meant — and look at what they show before you touch the plan. That's the pattern finding its own edges. What you read is the finish line you can stand at.
cells.sheetLine: The whole shape lands, and you get to look before you move.
cells.verb: seeing a thing whole until nothing in it is hidden
cells.place: the place where what's finished gets let go of, and the door out is the one you just came through

cells.tense: You are bracing for a completion that cannot be scheduled yet, and reading endings into whatever is still open.
cells.act: let the impulse start without a plan
cells.ask: Start something with no plan attached — a first sentence, a sketch, a call — and stop there. It doesn't need a purpose yet, and nothing has to come of it today.
cells.core:
You can see all of it ahead — except now it's more than is there, and whole shapes get closed before they've been made. The end gets known in advance, so nothing new is allowed to arrive, and finishing keeps happening early, in the wrong order. A mind that used to serve the work is now standing over it.

What loosens it isn't more knowing. Catch the start of something and keep it unaimed — let a thing be nothing in particular for one minute, no plan pinned to it. That's the freshest move available this week: let a thing begin without you already seeing its end. The finish you were bracing for keeps its own timing.
cells.sheetLine: You're seeing the ending before the work has a chance to make one.

cells.tense: A process of understanding finished and you are still standing at the door it opened.
cells.act: define the seed of what will be built, in one line
cells.ask: Write one line for what's next — what it's for, just the one. No steps, no shape it will take. Then the pen goes down for the night.
cells.core:
Reading a whole thing at once is in you. Where creation is concerned, though, things have gone quiet: nothing is being let go of, so nothing new gets to start. The understanding of whatever it was is complete, and the move into what comes after it didn't happen. Counting or willing it back won't do it. The careful, watchful place isn't slow — it's unhooked, and it can't be pressured into landing.

Something small and physical is what this wants. Hold one line in your hand before you invest anything in it: name, in a single line, what the next thing is for. Not the form, not the steps — the seed. Defining that much is enough of a landing for one night.
cells.sheetLine: The understanding finished, and you're still at the door it opened.

cells.tense: You're living in the middle of a whole turning of your life and telling it as weather.
cells.act: take the turning as it comes
cells.ask: Name one turning you've already taken — a thing that changed and you moved with it — in a plain sentence. Write it down and read it back once. Nothing needs deciding after.
cells.core:
You've been meeting what arrives as it arrives, over and over, and your account of it has you standing still while things happen around you. Whole situations get read at a glance; the next move is already known. You talk about it as timing, as things lining up, as being in some phase — and the one who kept landing on time is left out of the telling.

One turning you've already taken, named plainly, puts the writer back in the story. Not fate, not the sign of the times: you, noticing what was arriving and meeting it. After that, nothing needs deciding. The one who named it is the one who turned.
cells.sheetLine: You've been meeting what arrives, and calling it the times.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim I caught: writing that the total seeing is wanted, that this person is holding anything out of view, or that they chose their distance — the record says the capacity is present and running, and past-anchored, and it does not say what that costs or why. A reader could reasonably say 'I'm not standing at any door; this just isn't my season.' The ask still works if I'm wrong — it names a form for one thing they're already finishing, and they can do it tonight regardless of whether the diagnosis fits. The sentence that serves the writer, not them: 'creation is your home.' Cut it. Also cut, on rereading, two clauses about other people catching the seeing themselves — nothing in the record says they see it, only that the work lands.
